This page is about building and deploying the cloud package, plus day-2 operations against a live environment. Local development lives in the Development Guide.

What "operating" means here

There are two delivery modes:

  • Local. task deploy against the kind cluster. Used by developers and CI.
  • Cloud. A Zarf package built once, then deployed to one or more k3s clusters. This is the production-shaped path.

For phase order and rollout dependencies, see Architecture. The same phases apply in both modes.

Cloud package build

The cloud Zarf package mirrors task deploy:cloud. It renders each phase aggregator into a separate manifest and stitches them together with ordering hints.
task zarf:package:cloud

What the task does, in order:

  1. Copies ../zarf/cloud/zarf.template.yaml to .build/zarf/cloud/zarf.yaml.
  2. Renders each infra-phase1 bundle to its own manifest under .build/zarf/cloud/manifests/infra-phase1/. Splitting per bundle keeps each Helm-rendered manifest under the Kubernetes Secret size limit.
  3. Renders infra-phase2, monitoring, and opendefense to single manifests.
  4. Runs zarf dev find-images so the package self-describes its image list. The task supplies a placeholder hostname (placeholder.invalid) so discovery stays non-interactive.
  5. Appends the CloudNativePG init image (ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql:18.0-system-trixie) by hand. CNPG references the image dynamically, and find-images doesn't detect that reference.
  6. Calls zarf package create to produce zarf-package-opendefense-cloud-<arch>-1.0.0.tar.zst at the repo root.

Architecture defaults to amd64. Override it with:
task zarf:package:cloud ZARF_ARCHITECTURE=arm64

ZARF_YOLO=true strips the image list and sets metadata.yolo: true in the package. The target cluster then pulls images directly from their original registries. That's useful for environments with egress and no need for Zarf's image relocation. See ../zarf/cloud/README.md for the full task contract.

Cloud deploy

zarf package deploy uses whatever kube context the shell sees, so point KUBECONFIG at the right file before deploying. Pass OPENDEFENSE_HOST either via --set or interactively.

KUBECONFIG=k3s-azure.yaml zarf package deploy \
  "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/zarf-package-opendefense-cloud-amd64-1.0.0.tar.zst" \
  --set OPENDEFENSE_HOST=example.dev.pvarki.fi \
  --confirm

Zarf substitutes ###ZARF_VAR_OPENDEFENSE_HOST### everywhere the cloud overlays reference the host (ingress hostnames, app config). The phases deploy in declared order, with health checks between them:

  • infra-phase1. CNPG, cert-manager, Keycloak operator, External Secrets, Traefik, Grafana operator.
  • infra-phase2. trust-manager and cloud ClusterIssuers.
  • monitoring. Grafana, Loki, Alloy, Prometheus.
  • opendefense. CFSSL → PKI → opendefense-system → Battlelog → TAK → MTX.

task deploy:_apply enforces the same ordering for local. If a phase fails its health check, Zarf stops and surfaces which deployment didn't reach Ready.

Day-2 operations

Pre-flight before any change

kubectl config current-context        # confirm you are on the right cluster
kubectl get nodes                     # nodes Ready?
kubectl get pods -A | grep -v Running # anything stuck?

Re-deploying after a manifest change

For local, edit and then task deploy. For cloud, rebuild the package (task zarf:package:cloud) and run zarf package deploy again. Zarf is idempotent and reconciles what already exists.

Rotating secrets

Secrets are pulled in via external-secrets-operator from the configured secret store, so rotate them at the source. Then either let the ExternalSecret refresh interval pull the new value, or annotate the ExternalSecret to force a sync. Don't edit the synced Secret directly. The operator overwrites direct edits.

Renewing the internal CA

The cluster CA is issued by opendefense-cfssl, and cert-manager renews leaf certificates automatically. If you need to rotate the root, plan ahead. Every namespace that consumes the bundle via trust-manager has to roll its consumers after the new bundle propagates.

Logs and metrics

Logs flow through Alloy → Loki. Metrics flow through Prometheus. Dashboards live in Grafana. All three live in the monitoring namespace. Per-service log formatters are set in each overlay (e.g. LOG_CONSOLE_FORMATTER=local in battlelog), so local development stays human-readable while cloud emits structured JSON.

Common failure modes

Symptom Likely cause Where to look
zarf package deploy fails on phase-1 health check An operator didn't reach Ready in time kubectl describe deployment ... in the affected namespace
Helm-managed resource refuses to apply The cloud overlay tried to remove meta.helm.sh/* labels but the source still has them The patches: block in k8s/main/cloud/opendefense/kustomization.yaml
Zarf package build fails with "secret too big" A bundle's rendered manifest crossed 1 MiB Split it. Add a new subfolder under k8s/main/cloud/infra-phase1/bundles/
TAK clients cannot connect Port 8089 or 8443 not reachable, or mTLS cert chain wrong Check Traefik routes and the tak overlay
New product is missing from RM UI MW_PRODUCTS not updated, or miniwerk didn't re-run kubectl -n opendefense-system logs job/opendefense-miniwerk

Tearing down

  • Local: task down deletes the kind cluster.
  • Cloud: zarf package remove opendefense-cloud --confirm (with the right KUBECONFIG). Be deliberate. This removes the platform from the cluster.

What lives where

Concern File / path
Phase composition k8s/main/{local,cloud}/{infra-phase1,infra-phase2,monitoring,opendefense}/kustomization.yaml
Rollout wait gates taskfile.yaml, deploy:_apply
Zarf package definition zarf/cloud/zarf.template.yaml
Cloud package build flow taskfile.yaml, zarf:package:cloud
